title: Plania · Intelligent commercial and logistics planning
description: Connect the ERP you already have and find out what to discount, what to restock, what to re-price and how to route deliveries. An AI copilot on your real data. 7-day full trial, no card required.
hero_badge: For distributors, wholesalers and retailers in Uruguay and Latin America
hero_sub: Plania connects to the ERP you already have and tells you what to discount, what to restock, what to re-price and how to route deliveries. With a copilot that answers using your real numbers and hands you the report in PDF, Word or Excel.
hero_nota: No card required. Every feature enabled. Your data never leaves your machine.

plat_h: What it does for your business, every single day
plat_sub: This is not one more dashboard. Every screen ends in a concrete decision, with the reasoning in money.
f1_d: Zureo, Memory, Tango, Bejerman, Odoo, SAP Business One, or whatever PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQL Server/Oracle/SQLite/CSV you already run. It auto-detects your columns even when they are named differently. No migration, no consultants.
f2_d: "Which items should I discount this week?" "What do I restock today?" It answers by computing against your database and shows the table it used. It does not invent numbers.
f3_d: It spots the stock that stopped moving and works out a fair discount, never below cost plus 8%. It tells you exactly how much tied-up cash you release.
f4_d: It cross-checks real turnover against each supplier's lead time and tells you what to buy today, how much, and how much revenue is at risk if you wait.
f5_d: It finds the products selling below their category margin and suggests the new price with the monthly impact already calculated.
f6_d: It builds the day's routes per vehicle while minimising kilometres, with or without coordinates in your data. Export the route sheet and the truck rolls.
f7_d: It surfaces the cross-selling you are losing: which categories similar businesses buy in other zones and yours still does not.
f8_d: Every analysis and every copilot answer comes out as PDF, Word and Excel, ready to send to the owner, the buyer or the sales rep on the route.
erps_h: Your ERP, with nothing to map by hand
erps_sub: There is no separate Plania per system. There is an auto-mapper that recognises how each one names its columns, so the connection sets itself up.
erp1_d: Zureo runs in the cloud, so there is no on-premise database to connect to directly. Export stock, sales or customers to Excel or CSV from within Zureo itself, and Plania maps the columns on its own.
erp2_d: If Memory lets you export to Excel or CSV, that is the fastest start. If you have direct access to its database, Plania connects with nothing more than the connection string.
erp3_d: Tango installations usually run on a local database. With a read-only user for that database, Plania connects directly — no exports, no middleman.
erp4_d: Same story with Bejerman: if your installation runs locally, you connect directly to its database. Plania still detects the columns even if your install renamed them.
erps_metodo: The rest is handled by the auto-mapper: 177 typical column names from these systems plus Odoo, SAP Business One and generic databases — código, artículo, existencia, rubro, cardcode, itemcode, docdate and their variants. If your system uses a name that is not on the list yet, it gets added and keeps working.
sug_h: Five decisions, with the real number behind each one
sug_sub: Not charts — the five questions a distributor owner asks every week, each one with a real example from the demo dataset.
s1_t: Overstock → a discount with a real floor
s1_d: It spots the stock that stopped moving and works out the discount, never below cost plus 8%. Real example: “Lácteos Oro 395” has 584 units sitting for 113 days — UYU 106,183 tied up in that product alone. Across the full dataset, it frees up UYU 1,430,318.
s2_d: It cross-checks real turnover against each supplier's lead time. Real example: “Bebidas Eco 558” has 6 days of stock left and the supplier takes 8 — UYU 80,607/month of revenue at risk if it is not reordered today. Across the dataset, UYU 1,132,051 is at risk.
s3_d: It finds products selling below their category's margin. Real example: “Lácteos Clásico 736” sells at a 14% margin against a 25% category average — raising the price 14.7% adds UYU 5,765/month. Across the dataset, that is UYU 96,384/month.
s4_d: It compares which categories similar businesses buy, zone by zone. Real example: in Punta del Este, only 67% of Almacén-type businesses buy Limpieza products versus 99% across the rest of the dataset — a whole category nobody is offering there.
s5_t: Winning back customers who stopped buying
s5_d: It compares each customer's usual buying rhythm against how long it has been since their last order. Real example: “Almacén García” used to buy UYU 207,803 and has gone 52 days without ordering. Across the dataset, UYU 886,629 sits in customers worth calling back.
sug_nota: All five examples come from running Plania's real engines on its demo dataset (synthetic data, not an actual customer) — so you can see the level of detail before connecting your own.

impl_description: A partner program for consultants and technicians who connect ERPs. You keep the full implementation fee plus a 20% recurring commission for as long as the client stays active.
impl_badge: For consultants and technicians who already work with ERPs
impl_sub: You are the one going into the client's database, mapping the columns and getting Plania running. The client pays you the full implementation fee. And for as long as they keep using Plania, you keep earning a commission — with no time limit.
impl_paso1_d: Connect the client's ERP (direct database or an exported Excel/CSV), check the auto-mapping, and build the first batch of suggestions with them in the room. It is the same work you already do with other tools.
impl_paso2_t: 2. You get paid for the implementation
impl_paso2_d: You invoice the client directly, in the USD 450–950 range depending on the size of their database. That income is 100% yours — Plania does not touch a cent of it.
impl_paso3_t: 3. You get paid the commission, every month
impl_paso3_d: For as long as the client keeps paying their subscription, you get a percentage. You do not need to keep working there: it is paid for as long as the client stays active.
impl_comision_sub: Simple, no fine print: two numbers, and they go up with volume.
impl_c1_d: You charge it directly, following Plania's published price guide (USD 450–950).
impl_c2_d: Of the monthly subscription (Starter or Pro) for every client you implemented, for as long as they stay active.
impl_c3_d: The recurring commission goes up automatically once you cross that volume. No need to ask.
impl_ejemplo_h: What that looks like in numbers
impl_ejemplo_d: Ten clients on the Pro plan (USD 129/month) leave you USD 258 a month in recurring commission — on top of what you already charged for each implementation. It is income that keeps coming in even in a month you implemented no one new.

impl_r2: Accountants or firms that serve distributors and retailers
impl_r3: No exclusivity and no minimum client count required to start
impl_r4: You choose your own clients: Plania does not step into that business relationship
